newsitem.title: UK: UK Sept gas output up by 26 pct from Aug - Woodmac.
newsitem.headline: UK Sept gas output up by 26 pct from Aug - Woodmac.

text.p: UK natural gas production in September increased by 26 percent over the August level, marking the beginning of the seasonal upturn at the beginning of winter, according to consultants Wood Mackenzie.
Production averaged 5,944 million cubic feet a day (MMcfd) in September, up from 4,735 Mmcfd in August. It was also an increase of 737 MMcfd from September 1995.
Average production for the year October 1995 to September 1996 stood at 8,050 MMcfd, up by 19 percent from the 1994/1995 average. Woodmac attributes this to increased use of gas for power generation.
Increased demand and the completion of maintenance led to the resumption of production from the giant Morecambe Bay fields in September after a three month period when output stopped completely.
A number of other fields, including Clipper, Leman, Ravenspurn North and Victor also increased production to meet rising demand.
